text:
**My pick: Anker 735 Charger (Nano II 65W)**, $29.99 at Newegg: https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3

- It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A, and either USB-C port delivers 65W to a single device. That's enough for a MacBook Air, Dell XPS 13 or similar (per [Anker's spec page](https://service.anker.com/product-description/a085g000004x2BVAAY)).
- With a laptop and phone together on the two USB-C ports, it splits 45W + 20W. Put the laptop on USB-C 1.
- It supports PPS for Samsung phones, and it's sold by Anker's official store with an 18-month warranty ([Newegg listing](https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3)).
- Anker's 65W 3-port charger is the Editor's Choice in both [Laptopbee's 65W roundup](https://www.laptopbee.com/best-65w-usb-c-chargers/) and [its laptop charger guide](https://www.laptopbee.com/best-usb-c-laptop-chargers/). Those reviews describe the Anker 65W 3-Port GaN II charger, which I'm treating as the same product family as the Nano II 735. I can't confirm that from the results.

**Alternatives**

- **UGREEN Nexode Pro 65W:** [Smart Gadget Kit's top pick](https://smartgadgetkit.com/best-gan-charger/). It has 3 ports in a 113g body, verified 65W from a single port, and US/UK/EU plug heads in the box, which is good for international travel. The results gave me no direct purchase link, so the review page is the closest I can offer.
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2-pack):** $49.99 for two chargers, so you get one for home and one for your bag. It has the same 45W + 20W split and supports PPS. No discount code worked when tested. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) (affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy; the price is the same for you). Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-65w-gan-charger-laptop-phone-2026-review-anker-ugreen-baseus).

**Caveats**

- If your laptop needs a full 65W while you also charge a phone, any 65W charger will slow the laptop. For that, look at a 100W model such as the Anker Prime 100W, which Smart Gadget Kit recommends for 14" and 16" MacBook Pros.
- With all three ports in use, power drops further, so use two ports at most for the best laptop speed.
- Check your laptop's charging requirement. A few gaming or workstation laptops need more than 65W.
